title: Long-term outcome of patients with inherited metabolic diseases after diagnosis by expanded newborn screening
summary: As part of newborn screening, a blood test is carried out a few days after birth for inborn errors of metabolism, among other diseases. In the present study, children and adolescents with a congenital metabolic disorder who were found by the newborn screening and subsequently confirmed are followed up until adulthood. The collected data is recorded in a register.  In particular, the study analyses data on the physical and mental development of the children, the course of the disease and the therapy. The aim is to show how the children benefit from newborn screening and early therapy.

criteria:
Inclusion criteria:
All patients, since 1999, in which an inherited metabolic disease was suspected by newborn screening in Heidelberg and subsequently confirmed by further analysis. 
Additionally, patients identified by another German newborn screening center may be included (Start 01.03.2016) if the relevant data about newborn screening and confirmation diagnosis is available. Furthermore, patients not detected by newborn screening (false negative) may be included.
Exclusion criteria:
No informed consent except for deceased patients.
